reason: Schema matches and weather labels stay plausible, but the synthetic January sample is much warmer than the original winter slice, with duplicate dates and no snow records.
Columns and numeric scales are close, but the generated timestamps are random across months with arbitrary seconds instead of a regular hourly sequence from the original.
Format matches, but prices are shifted much lower and the monthly dates jump across many years with duplicates, so the time-series structure is only loosely preserved.
The OHLCV schema matches, but many market relationships are broken: highs can fall below opens, lows are far too low, volumes are inflated, and duplicate dates appear.
Species identity fields match perfectly, but county_id collapses to a single value and habitat percentages are much higher than the mostly near-zero original distribution.
Headers match, but several categorical fields are garbled or shifted (for example steak prep values contain tab-joined text), 'Do you eat steak?' is blank, and row semantics are damaged.
This preserves the symbol, monthly dates, row count, and overall stock-series structure well; the main issue is a lower price distribution than the original MSFT sample.
Numeric trip fields are somewhat plausible, but zone and borough fields are broken, short trips span multiple days, and location relationships are not preserved.
Schema, row count, value ranges, and restaurant-style categorical values are all very close; the synthetic sample keeps realistic bill-tip-size relationships with only minor distribution drift.
Columns line up, but several discrete fields become continuous floats, embarked values disappear, text fields are partially merged, and important passenger relationships are weakened.
JSON structure, series labels, row count, and most numeric distributions are close, but the generated date field no longer aligns with the year/month values and jumps into unrelated calendar years.
Numeric magnitudes are in the right ballpark, but state/code fields are malformed and shifted, which breaks the core state-to-measure relationships despite the matching schema.
Airport traffic uses the right columns and plausible airport-like text, but airport/city/state combinations are mismatched, state is blank, and counts become unrealistic fractional values.

The structure and numeric ranges are solid, with valid calendar-style values and realistic birth counts, but the original January-only slice becomes a mixed-month sample and loses its ordered sequence.
Generated values stay in a believable births domain with matching columns and row count, though months and dates no longer follow the original ordered January subset.
The city dataset keeps the right schema and plausible US-style names and coordinates, but populations are inflated and the city-to-location relationships are not reliably preserved.
Majors and categories remain in the same general domain, but some major-category assignments are wrong and core numeric relationships like Total versus Men/Women are not preserved.
